title: Driverless cars
paragraphs: As the relentless pace of technology continues to advance, companies must adapt or get left behind. One of the key areas of contention these days is the driverless car. Autonomous cars have long been featured in science fiction movies and books, but in recent years they have moved from a pipe dream to a reality.
The development of the autonomous car actually started in the 1920s, but it wasn't until the 1980s that the first prototypes were successfully created, one of which was designed by Mercedes-Benz.

Since then the technology has gone from strength to strength and these days many companies are jumping on the bandwagon. Uber is the latest to announce its plan to unroll a fleet of driverless cars. It follows Apple and Ford, who have announced similar plans, and Google and Tesla, who already have autonomous cars on the road.

Two questions arise: Do we really need them? And are they really safe? Advocates of driverless cars would argue 'yes' to both. Vehicular autonomy, if perfected, could lead to much safer road conditions for all, lower insurance costs and enhance mobility for the elderly, the sick and those with disabilities. They would also allow roads to increase their capacity between 200 - 400%.

Perfection, though, seems to be just out of reach at the moment. To date Google's self-driving car, launched in 2012, has had 14 minor accidents. Even worse, Tesla's Autopilot has caused one fatality in 2015, where the vehicle simply did not see the obstacle.

While the technology exists, driverless cars and full vehicular autonomy is still embryonic. That said, you can rest assured that further development in the field is inevitable. And what's the future? Well, George Marcus, co-founder of Geometric Intelligence — Uber's autonomous development department — imagines a world of flying cars taking us to work. He says "They're going to allow people to take long commutes at 75 or 150 mph where you'd otherwise get stuck in traffic. It's really, in a not-too-distant future, going to be something that is practical."

vocabulary.entry: contention [n.] /kənˈtenʃən/ 争论；争执；竞争
vocabulary.example: The issue is a point of contention between the two parties.
vocabulary.translation: 这个问题是两党之间的争论点。

vocabulary.entry: pipe dream [n.] /ˈpaɪp driːm/ 不切实际的幻想；白日梦
vocabulary.example: His plan to become a millionaire overnight is a pipe dream.
vocabulary.translation: 他想一夜之间成为百万富翁的计划是不切实际的幻想。

vocabulary.entry: jumping on the bandwagon [phr.] /ˈdʒʌmpɪŋ ɒn ðə ˈbændwæɡən/ 跟风；赶时髦 (固定搭配)
vocabulary.example: Many companies are jumping on the bandwagon of artificial intelligence.
vocabulary.translation: 许多公司都在跟风人工智能。

vocabulary.entry: unroll [v.] /ʌnˈrəʊl/ 展开；推出 (此处指推出车队)
vocabulary.example: The company will unroll its new product line next month.
vocabulary.translation: 该公司将于下月推出其新产品线。

vocabulary.entry: embryonic [adj.] /ˌembriˈɒnɪk/ 萌芽的；初期的
vocabulary.example: The technology is still in its embryonic stage.
vocabulary.translation: 这项技术仍处于萌芽阶段。

vocabulary.entry: adapt to [phr.] /əˈdæpt tuː/ 适应 (固定搭配)
vocabulary.example: Animals adapt to their environment over time.
vocabulary.translation: 动物随着时间推移适应环境。

vocabulary.entry: get left behind [phr.] /ɡet left bɪˈhaɪnd/ 被甩在后面；落后 (固定搭配)
vocabulary.example: If you don't study, you'll get left behind.
vocabulary.translation: 如果你不学习，就会被甩在后面。

vocabulary.example: The business has grown from strength to strength.
vocabulary.translation: 这家企业日益壮大。

vocabulary.entry: arise [v.] /əˈraɪz/ 出现；产生
vocabulary.example: Problems may arise if we are not careful.
vocabulary.translation: 如果我们不小心，可能会出现问题。

vocabulary.entry: lead to [phr.] /liːd tuː/ 导致；引起 (固定搭配)
vocabulary.example: Smoking can lead to cancer.
vocabulary.translation: 吸烟会导致癌症。

vocabulary.entry: enhance mobility [phr.] /ɪnˈhɑːns məʊˈbɪləti/ 提高出行能力；增强移动性 (固定搭配)
vocabulary.example: Wheelchairs enhance mobility for disabled people.
vocabulary.translation: 轮椅提高了残疾人的出行能力。

vocabulary.entry: out of reach [phr.] /aʊt əv riːtʃ/ 够不着；遥不可及 (固定搭配)
vocabulary.example: The goal seemed out of reach.
vocabulary.translation: 这个目标似乎遥不可及。

vocabulary.entry: to date [phr.] /tə deɪt/ 到目前为止；迄今为止 (固定搭配)
vocabulary.example: To date, no cure has been found.
vocabulary.translation: 到目前为止，还没有找到治愈方法。

vocabulary.entry: rest assured [phr.] /rest əˈʃʊəd/ 放心；确信无疑 (固定搭配)
vocabulary.example: Rest assured that we will do our best.
vocabulary.translation: 请放心，我们会尽力的。

vocabulary.entry: be inevitable [phr.] /biː ɪˈnevɪtəbəl/ 是不可避免的 (固定搭配)
vocabulary.example: Change is inevitable in life.
vocabulary.translation: 生活中的变化是不可避免的。

vocabulary.entry: take sb to work [phr.] /teɪk ˈsʌmbədi tə wɜːk/ 送某人去上班 (固定搭配)
vocabulary.example: He takes his wife to work every morning.
vocabulary.translation: 他每天早上送妻子去上班。

vocabulary.entry: get stuck in [phr.] /ɡet stʌk ɪn/ 陷入；困在 (固定搭配)
vocabulary.example: We got stuck in traffic for two hours.
vocabulary.translation: 我们堵车堵了两个小时。

vocabulary.entry: a not-too-distant future [phr.] /ə nɒt tuː ˈdɪstənt ˈfjuːtʃə/ 不太遥远的未来 (固定搭配)
vocabulary.example: Flying cars may be a reality in the not-too-distant future.
vocabulary.translation: 在不太遥远的将来，飞行汽车可能成为现实。

vocabulary.entry: feature in [phr.] /ˈfiːtʃər ɪn/ 在……中出现 (固定搭配)
vocabulary.example: The actor featured in several blockbuster films.
vocabulary.translation: 这位演员出演了几部大片。

vocabulary.entry: minor accident [n.] /ˈmaɪnər ˈæksɪdənt/ 小事故
vocabulary.example: He had a minor accident but was not injured.
vocabulary.translation: 他出了一次小事故，但没有受伤。

vocabulary.entry: prototype [n.] /ˈprəʊtətaɪp/ 原型；样机
vocabulary.example: The company is testing a prototype of the new car.
vocabulary.translation: 这家公司正在测试新车的原型。

vocabulary.entry: vehicular [adj.] /viːˈhɪkjʊlə/ 车辆的；用车辆运输的
vocabulary.example: Vehicular traffic is heavy during rush hour.
vocabulary.translation: 高峰时段车辆交通繁忙。

vocabulary.entry: capacity [n.] /kəˈpæsəti/ 能力；容量
vocabulary.example: The stadium has a seating capacity of 50,000.
vocabulary.translation: 这个体育场可容纳5万人。

vocabulary.entry: fatality [n.] /fəˈtæləti/ 死亡事故；死亡
vocabulary.example: The accident resulted in one fatality.
vocabulary.translation: 这起事故导致一人死亡。
